questions.question: Which of the following crops is most suitable for black soil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) Cotton**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cotton** is the most suitable crop for black soil.
 
• Black soil, also known as **Regur soil**, is ideal for cotton cultivation due to its moisture-retentive properties.
 
• This type of soil is predominantly found in the **Deccan Plateau** region, including parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• Black soil is rich in **calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime**, which are essential nutrients for cotton growth.
 
• The soil's high clay content helps in holding moisture, which is beneficial during dry periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Black soil is also suitable for crops like **soybean, sorghum, and sunflower** but is most renowned for cotton cultivation.
 
• Cotton is often referred to as the "**King of Fibers**" due to its global economic importance.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of cotton in the world, contributing significantly to the country's agricultural economy.
 
• Historically, the **Indus Valley Civilization** is known to have cultivated cotton as early as 3000 BCE.
 
• Cotton cultivation requires a warm climate with moderate rainfall, which is typically found in regions with black soil.

• **Aus** is sown in summer and harvested in autumn.

• **Boro** is cultivated in the winter season and harvested in summer.
 
• These terms are specific to the traditional rice farming practices in regions like West Bengal and Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Rice farming in India is highly dependent on the monsoon season, and the crop requires a lot of water for cultivation.
 
• The Green Revolution in India significantly boosted rice production, making the country self-sufficient in food grains.
 
• Modern techniques and high-yield varieties have also contributed to increased rice production in India.

questions.question: Which regulatory body in India is responsible for overseeing and regulating Micro Finance Institutions?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the regulatory body responsible for overseeing and regulating Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) in India.
 
• RBI provides guidelines and frameworks to ensure the smooth functioning of MFIs and protect the interests of borrowers.
 
• MFIs play a crucial role in providing financial services to the underserved and unbanked population in rural and semi-urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** was established on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• It serves as the central bank of India, responsible for regulating the issue and supply of the Indian rupee.
 
• The RBI also manages the country's main payment systems and works to promote its economic development.
 
• In addition to regulating MFIs, the RBI oversees other financial institutions, including commercial banks, cooperative banks, and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs).
 
• The RBI's primary functions include monetary policy regulation, financial supervision, and payment system oversight.

questions.question: Which of the following is the legislative organ of the Union Government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Parliament** is the legislative organ of the Union Government of India.
 
• It is composed of the **President** and the two houses: **Rajya Sabha (Council of States)** and **Lok Sabha (House of the People)**.
 
• The Parliament is responsible for enacting laws, discussing national issues, and overseeing the work of the executive branch.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the democratic governance of the country by representing the interests of the citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian Parliament** is bicameral, consisting of the **Rajya Sabha** and the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, while the members of the **Lok Sabha** are directly elected by the people of India for a term of five years.
 
• The **President of India** is an integral part of the Parliament and has the power to summon and prorogue either house of Parliament or to dissolve the Lok Sabha.
 
• Legislative proposals are introduced in the form of bills in either house of Parliament and must be passed by both houses and receive the President's assent to become law.

questions.question: Due to rapid urbanisation, the human lifestyle has changed severely; obesity is a major health issue in such condition. Which of the following is a reason for obesity?

options.text: Excessive intake of high calorie foods
Lack of vitamins in regular diet

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Excessive intake of high calorie foods**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Excessive intake of high calorie foods** is a primary reason for obesity, especially in rapidly urbanizing areas.
 
• Urbanization often leads to lifestyle changes that include increased consumption of fast food, sugary beverages, and other high-calorie, low-nutrient foods.
 
• This dietary shift, combined with reduced physical activity, contributes significantly to weight gain and obesity.
 
• Obesity is associated with various health issues such as diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and hypertension.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Obesity is defined as having a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher.
 
• Urban environments often provide less opportunity for physical activity due to sedentary jobs and limited access to recreational areas.
 
• Public health initiatives aimed at reducing obesity often focus on promoting healthier eating habits and increasing physical activity.
 
• Other factors contributing to obesity include genetics, metabolism, behavior, and culture.
 
• Addressing obesity requires a multifaceted approach including education, policy changes, and community support.

__
 
• **Shree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam** was founded in Kerala.
 
• SNDP Yogam is a social organization established to promote the teachings and principles of **Shree Narayana Guru**, a renowned social reformer and spiritual leader.
 
• The organization plays a significant role in the social and educational upliftment of the Ezhava community in Kerala.
 
• SNDP Yogam has been instrumental in advocating for social equality and fighting against the caste-based discrimination prevalent in Kerala during the early 20th century.

• He emphasized the values of equality, education, and social reform, and his teachings continue to inspire many.
 
• SNDP Yogam was founded in 1903 to institutionalize the reform movements initiated by Shree Narayana Guru.
 
• The organization also focuses on educational initiatives, running several schools and colleges to provide quality education to the underprivileged sections of society.
 
• SNDP Yogam has played a crucial role in the socio-economic development of Kerala and continues to be a significant force in promoting social justice.

questions.question: Shama Bhate received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award - 2021 (given in February 2023) for her contribution to which dance form of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shama Bhate** received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award - 2021 for her outstanding contribution to the dance form **Kathak**.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is a prestigious recognition given by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**, India's National Academy of Music, Dance, and Drama.
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance and has origins in the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as **Kathakars** or storytellers.
 
• This dance form is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and facial expressions to convey stories.
 
• Shama Bhate is renowned for her contributions to Kathak, both as a performer and as a teacher, and has trained numerous students in this classical art form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** was established in 1952 and is the first national academy for the performing arts set up by the Republic of India.
 
• The awards given by the Akademi are considered among the highest national recognitions conferred on practicing artists, gurus, and scholars in the field of performing arts.
 
• Recipients of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award are honored for their sustained individual achievements and contributions to their respective fields.
 
• The award comprises a **cash prize, a citation, and a Tamrapatra (a copper plaque)**.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi also functions as an advisory body to the Ministry of Culture in the Government of India in the task of promoting and preserving the performing arts of the country.

questions.question: Which of the following Indus Valley sites is now located in Pakistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harappa**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harappa** is one of the major sites of the Indus Valley Civilization and is currently located in Pakistan.
 
• The site was discovered in the 1920s and has provided significant insights into the urban planning and social structure of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• **Lothal**, **Alamgirpur**, and **Kalibangan** are other notable sites of the Indus Valley Civilization, but they are located in India.
 
• Harappa is situated in the Punjab province of Pakistan, near the Ravi River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as the Harappan Civilization, was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, dating back to around 2500 BCE.
 
• It was characterized by advanced city planning, including well-laid-out streets, drainage systems, and large communal buildings.
 
• Artifacts found at Harappa include pottery, seals, weights, and tools, which indicate a highly developed trade and craft industry.
 
• The decline of the Indus Valley Civilization around 1900 BCE remains a topic of research and debate among historians and archaeologists.

questions.question: Which of the following peninsular rivers of India is a west flowing river?

• **Narmada** is one of the major rivers in India that flows westwards.
 
• It is the **fifth longest river** in the Indian subcontinent and the third longest river that flows entirely within India.
 
• The Narmada River flows through the states of **Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat** before emptying into the Arabian Sea.
 
• It is often referred to as the **"Life Line of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat"** due to its extensive contribution to the water supply and agriculture in these states.

• It forms the traditional boundary between North India and South India.
 
• The river basin is known for its rich biodiversity and is home to several **wildlife sanctuaries**.
 
• The Narmada Valley is also known for its **cultural and historical significance**, with several ancient temples and archaeological sites located along its course.
 
• The river has been a source of inspiration for many poets and writers in Indian literature.
 
• The **Sardar Sarovar Dam** on the Narmada is one of the largest and most controversial dam projects in India.

questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution of India deal with the Union and its territory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 1 - 4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Articles 1 - 4** of the Constitution of India deal with the Union and its territory.
 
• These articles define the name and territory of the Union, admission or establishment of new states, formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
 
• Article 1 declares India as a Union of States, emphasizing its indestructible nature.
 
• Article 2 empowers the Parliament to admit or establish new states into the Union.
 
• Article 3 provides the procedure for the formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
 
• Article 4 specifies that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 for the admission/establishment of new states or alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states are not to be considered amendments of the Constitution under Article 368.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.
